newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off as bolivar yo-yos.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off as bolivar yo-yos.

text.p: Confused by a wildly-gyrating Venezuelan bolivar and put off by a 12-hour strike at telephone company CANTV, investors shunned Caracas stocks, which closed off in shallow trade Monday.
"Investors are staying away because of uncertainty ... not least, nobody understands what the Central Bank is doing to the bolivar," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.
Volatile trade saw the bolivar open at 482/483 per dollar, then yo-yo between 491 and 476.00 per dollar.
"Who is going to invest in Venezuela when the foreign exchange market appears so confused?" said another broker.

The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index slipped 1.38 percent to end at 6,616.52 points as 15 million shares traded worth 3.6 billion bolivars ($7.7 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Merinvest's composite .MRCP index, which includes CANTV, meanwhile dropped 1.59 percent to end at 101.20.
"The CANTV work stoppage definitely dented the market," said Financorp broker Miguel Ortiz, who saw similarly slow sessions for the rest of the week.

CANTV said only 500 of the company's 17,300 workers joined the 12 hour walk-out, which began at 0600 local/1000 GMT, adding that operations were not affected. Neverthless, share prices slipped 29.00 bolivars to end at 2131.00.
Among total traded issues, 21 fell, six rose and 10 ended flat.
